chapter: Casa, Zeb Lenard and Little Joe
title: The Casa, a friend killed on the way to a gig, and a pay dispute
summary: Vincent recalls playing the Casa. He tells of a friend killed by a car before he could start a band, and of a leader paying him and John Casimir eight dollars a night while drummer Mason got more.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: ...Casa? Ask him about the Casa. What about Casa?

Casa? Casa? You're here talking in there. We used to play the Casa a lot of times too, you know. And I don't know but... ...if he had to come to my house that day, he might have been living today. When he first come back from California, he come to see me. And he say, what you doing, Dad? I said, nothing man, time. Kind of... ...dove down there. He says, uh... ...well, why don't you... ...we and you get together and get up a little four or five piece bag? I said, that's what I've been waiting for. I said, I think we can make it. And he told me all that. I said, all right, when will you be here tomorrow? The same, same time, I told him. And he told me, all right. But it's rain. Without the rain, he could, you know, come. If he had to come, he might have been living today. He didn't come. He was going somewhere else. And the automobile passed there, making six miles an hour. And he knocked with us from the rear to the corner. Kept him dead. His wife was staying over there to sell out the property, you know. He'd come back there to live, you know. He used to play clown up in South, too. There'd be only one brother that lived in the night, that's John. Yeah. He got a barber shop. Yeah, at First and Liberty. Yeah, bass. He was in the- Is he still in the house or somebody else had a movie? He played together a whole lot of time, too. And once they had a fellow named Nation played drum. Maen Dung and Charlie Hampton . They were talking about Charlie Hampton . He had to get to . So they got us together, you know. And then last night, he come up to talk about me and John Casimir, and I had John there with me. So I tell him, come and ask me, say, how much a nation pay you? I say, pay me eight. Quiet, I tell him, eight dollars a night. I say, how much you pay you, John? John say, eight. He said, listen, I try paying twelve dollars a night. I say, what? Twelve dollars a night. He said, you wonder how I knew he had your car in there and he gave me twelve. He said, this don't say nothing about it. I don't know how it was. He got together and he told John, he said, he's dead because he was no murdered. He said, you had to get somebody to come here near you. And John said, what? He said, that's a musician. I said, that ain't no funny musician. He said, you can't hear no murder. He said, if there ain't somebody here that can lead murder, I'll make that play. Everything you got in that band room. And he didn't, you know, he didn't know I knowed it. So, where I go, I, he got rid of John. So, that's why I told him, if he gets rid of John, he has to get rid of me. So, then I told him I was quick. Man, he paid me to come back. Well, that wasn't good. He lost his job. And I told him, I said, then you wasn't paying but eight dollars a month. He told him the mic when his job was paying quite a lot of the night. That made him do that, too. And Hans had taken his job, you see, for himself, you know. Mason just set out all the right. And Mason couldn't play nothing, but just hit on them drums. I said, I'm sorry. Ask him about what was Zeb's real name. What was Zeb's real name? Zeb, Zeb. Lenard. Lenard, yeah. Lenard, yeah. Lenard, yeah. Zeb Lenard. Zeb, Zeb. Zeb, Zeb.
